elements.element: The liability cap applies mutually to each party.
elements.evidence: The added paragraph applies to “each Party's total aggregate liability.”

elements.element: Liability is subject to a total aggregate cap.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly limits each party's “total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement.”

elements.element: The fee-based limb of the cap is calculated using fees both paid and payable.
elements.evidence: The clause includes amounts “paid or payable,” but uses all “aggregate amounts” under the Agreement rather than limiting the calculation to fees.

elements.element: The fee-based limb uses the 12 months preceding the claim.
elements.evidence: The lookback runs for 12 months preceding “the event giving rise to the claim,” which may differ materially from the 12 months preceding the claim itself.

elements.element: The alternative cap limb is USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: The second limb is expressly “USD 1,000,000.”

elements.element: The cap is the greater of the 12-month fee limb and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly uses “the greater of” limbs (a) and (b).

elements.element: Indirect damages are excluded mutually.
elements.evidence: Section 16.5 provides that “IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY” be liable for indirect damages, subject to its express exceptions.

elements.element: Consequential damages are excluded mutually.
elements.evidence: Section 16.5 provides that “IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY” be liable for consequential damages, subject to its express exceptions.

elements.element: Liability for breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: A party's breach of its confidentiality obligations under Article 10 is included in “Excluded Claims,” which are excepted from the aggregate cap.

elements.element: Liability for breach of data protection obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The definition of “Excluded Claims” contains no carve-out for data protection obligations.

elements.element: Liability for breach of security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The definition of “Excluded Claims” contains no carve-out for security obligations.

elements.element: Liability for indemnification obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Indemnification obligations under Sections 16.1 and 16.2 are included in “Excluded Claims” and therefore excluded from the aggregate cap.

elements.element: Liability arising from gross negligence is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Gross negligence is included in “Excluded Claims” and is also excepted from the consequential-damages limitation.

elements.element: Liability arising from wilful misconduct is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Willful misconduct is included in “Excluded Claims” and is also excepted from the consequential-damages limitation.

elements.element: Liability arising from fraud is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Fraud is expressly included in “Excluded Claims.”

elements.element: Liability arising from infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights is uncapped.
elements.evidence: A party's infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights is expressly included in “Excluded Claims.”

elements.element: The Customer's payment obligations are not treated as damages for purposes of the cap.
elements.evidence: The clause states that amounts payable by Ono under the Agreement do not constitute damages for purposes of the cap; Ono is the paying party in the cap formula.

elements.element: The total aggregate liability cap equals 12 months' fees.
elements.evidence: The cap is the greater of a 12-month payment measure and USD 1,000,000, so it can exceed 12 months' fees; it also uses aggregate amounts rather than fees specifically.

elements.element: Liability for indemnification obligations is carved out from the cap.
elements.evidence: Indemnification obligations under Sections 16.1 and 16.2 are included in “Excluded Claims.”

elements.element: Liability for breach of confidentiality obligations is carved out from the cap.
elements.evidence: Breach of confidentiality obligations under Article 10 is included in “Excluded Claims.”

elements.element: Liability arising from gross negligence is carved out from the cap.
elements.evidence: Gross negligence is expressly included in “Excluded Claims.”

elements.evidence: Willful misconduct is expressly included in “Excluded Claims.”

result.reason: The redline is targeted and preserves unrelated terms, but it does not satisfy either complete position. The preferred position is missing uncapped data-protection and security claims, and its fee metric and lookback trigger differ from the required formula. The fallback fails because the USD 1,000,000 floor means the cap is not necessarily limited to 12 months' fees.
